1170:
The following signs types are prohibited throughout the City of Ringgold in all zone districts, unless otherwise noted.
4.1-1 Billboards signs. Such signs, even if the properties are zoned C-1, C-2, and I-1, shall be prohibited along the following designated corridors:
(a) Battlefield Parkway from its intersection with Highway 41 to its intersection with Smitherman Road;
(b) Highway 41 (Nashville Street) from its intersection with Cherokee Valley Road to its intersection with Battlefield Parkway;
(c) Highway 151 from its intersection with Interstate 75 to its intersection with Tennessee Street;
(d) Lafayette Street from its intersection with Nashville Street to its intersection with Highway 151.
4.1-2 Roof signs, including those hanging over a parapet wall.
4.1-3 Flashing signs.
4.1-4 Bench signs.
4.1-5 Abandoned signs.
4.1-6 Lighted, neon or luminous signs giving off light resulting in glare, blinding, or any other such adverse effect on traffic shall not be erected or maintained.
4.1-7 A sign which simulates an official traffic control or warning sign in such a manner as to confuse or mislead the traffic, or hide from view any traffic or street sign or signal.
4.1-8 Signs which emit or use in any manner any sound capable of being detected by a person with normal hearing that is moving as a pedestrian or within a motor vehicle along any road or highway.
4.1-9 Signs on public rights-of-way.
4.1-10 Signs erected, maintained, affixed, painted, drawn on any tree, rock, or other natural feature. It shall also be unlawful to post signs, upon any utility or telephone poles and traffic control devices.
4.1-11 No sign shall be erected or maintained which obstructs any fire escape, any means of ingress/egress or ventilation, or which prevents free passage from one part of a roof to any other part thereof; nor shall any sign be attached in any form shape or manner to a fire escape.
4.1-12 Portable signs, however, such a sign may be used on grand openings for a period not to exceed four weeks.
4.1-13 Animated signs that change sign copy more frequently than ten seconds.
4.1-14 Signs that contain words, pictures, or statements that are obscene as defined by O.C.G.A § 16-12-80.
4.1-15 Any sign or sign structure that is unsafe, or constitutes a hazard to safety or health by reason of inadequate maintenance, dilapidation, or abandonment, or is not kept in good repair, or is likely to cause electrical shocks to persons expected to come in contact with the sign or sign structure.
1171:
The following sign types require the issuance of permits unless otherwise stated by this ordinance.
4.2-1 Pylon/freestanding signs. Such signs shall only be located on property in multi-family residential, commercial (including shopping centers and multi-tenant buildings), or industrially zoned areas, unless otherwise stated. The display area of such signs shall not extend over a public right-of-way line or property line. Those pole signs having all of the display area eight feet six inches or more above ground level when measured from the grade at the right-of-way line may be erected so that the display areas abuts the right-of-way line. Signs with any portion of the display area less than eight feet six inches above ground level must be erected 12 feet from the right-of-way line. For C-1, C-2 and 1-1 the square footage of a pylon/freestanding sign shall be limited to 288 square feet for on-premises signs that have a minimum height of the bottom edge of sign greater than 20 above the ground. The square footage of a pylon/freestanding sign with the bottom edge of the sign greater than 20 feet in height above the ground shall not be included in the aggregate limit for the parcel.
(a) Multi-family residential developments, the total maximum sign display surface per sign shall be 128 square feet.
(b) On parcels zoned R-1 or R-2, the maximum size per sign is not greater than 16 square feet, not higher than six feet, and not located any closer than ten feet to any property line.
(c) In the C-3 zone district, where a conventional lot exists, the maximum size is 50 square feet and the maximum height is 25 feet, otherwise a freestanding sign is prohibited; in the O-1 zone district a freestanding sign is limited to a ground sign. See subsection 4.2-2.
4.2-2 Ground signs. Allowed in multi-family residential, commercial, and industrial zone districts, a ground sign is a freestanding sign, provided that it does not exceed 3.5 feet in height, and is no bigger than 18 square feet in area, measured on one side only. Ground signs must be set back at least three feet from the public right-of-way. A freestanding sign in the O-1 zone district shall be limited to a ground sign and the display area shall not exceed 16 square feet.
4.2-3 Wall. Wall signs (including signs attached flat against the wall and painted wall signs) shall be securely fastened by metal supports to the building surface along the sign's greatest dimension. They may project from the building 12 inches provided that, if they project more than four inches from the building surface, they shall maintain a clear height of eight feet six inches above the ground level. A wall sign may be permitted on an existing building which does not meet the setback requirement provided that the sign meets all other requirements of this section and is not located within the right-of-way. In the C-3 zone district, a wall sign shall be below the second floor of a multi-story building and the size of the display areas shall be limited to a maximum height of two feet six inches, but may extend the width of the building.
(a) Signs on the facades of the building. The total area of a wall sign on the exterior front surface of a business premise shall not exceed 20 percent of front surface of the business or 200 square feet, whichever is less. The total aggregate area of a wall signs on a side or rear surface of a business premises shall not exceed 25 percent of the exterior side or rear surface of the business respectively or 200 square feet, whichever is less. The maximum size of a wall sign for a residential dwelling is 16 square feet and for a multi-family residential project/development is 50 square feet.
(b) Larger buildings. A non-residential building containing an area of 50,000 square feet, or more, may have multiple wall signs on any facade of the building, not exceeding ten percent of any facade, but the total number of such signs count as one allowable sign per facade.
4.2-4 Window signs. The aggregate sign area (permanent and/or temporary window signs) shall not exceed 30 percent of the aggregate window area. Window signs on or above the second floor are prohibited except when a business has no ground floor frontage, then, in such event the provisions of this subsection 4.2-4 shall apply. Direct painted, gold leaf, or similar style, and hanging signs on the interior are allowed. Multiple and conforming window signs that are to be installed contemporaneously with each other may be included in a single permit application. The permit fee for such an application shall be based on the aggregate square footage of the signs.
4.2-5 Projecting signs. Projecting signs shall be securely fastened by metal supports to the building surface along the sign's greatest dimension. They may project from the building wall no more than four feet to the outside edge of the sign. Projecting signs are not permitted at the intersection of corners except at right angles to the building front, unless otherwise authorized by this ordinance.
(a) The maximum size of a projecting sign is 40 square feet in commercial and industrial zone districts where such signs are allowed. In the C-3 zone district, projecting signs may overhang the R/W as long as a clear height of eight feet six inches is maintained above the ground, a sidewalk, or pedestrian walkway. Projecting signs are prohibited on all residentially used and zoned properties.
4.2-6 Canopy signs or hanging signs. Such signs shall not exceed ten square feet in size and shall be not less than seven feet four inches above the ground at the lowest extremity of the sign. Such signage shall not be internally lighted.
(Ord. No. 2015-0928, § 1, 9-28-15; Ord. No. 2017-0925-02, § 5, 9-25-17)
1172:
Signage may periodically be needed for a short duration rather than permanent usage. These signs shall not be erected within the public right-of-way and shall be located on private property with the permission of the property owner. Only one permit shall be issued to cover all temporary signs. The maximum number of temporary permits to be issued to a single parcel in a multi-family, commercial, or industrial district shall be four per year for a period of time not to exceed 30 days for each permit issued. Not more than one special event permit shall be issued per calendar quarter per business premises.
Banners are allowable as temporary signs.
1173:
4.4-1 The following types of signs shall be exempt from the permit requirements of this ordinance:
(a) Freestanding sign, having a sign area of less than 16 square feet, provided it is not located in the public right-of-way, does not block vehicle sight visibility, does not exceed three feet in height if a ground sign, or if a pole sign, does not exceed six feet in height.
(b) Temporary window sign. Provided, however, the aggregate sign area shall not exceed 30 percent of the available window space.
(c) Seasonal displays, located outside of the public right-of-way that are erected for a maximum period of 60 days, not more than twice a year.
(d) Non-illuminated wall signs, not larger than two square feet.
(e) Temporary signs erected by schools and non-profit organizations.
(f) Temporary signs related to a newly opened business or special event shall be allowed for 30 days and its display areas shall be limited to 2.5 feet high and the length of the building facades.
4.4-2 Flagpoles in residentially zoned districts shall not exceed 25 feet in height or the height of the primary structure, whichever is less. Flagpoles in commercial or industrial zoned districts shall not exceed 60 feet in height. The dimensions of any flag shall not exceed 50 percent of the vertical height.
1174:
4.5-1 Residential districts.
(a) Platted residential subdivisions may erect one monument sign at each entrance to the subdivision. Such sign shall not exceed a height of five feet above the grade level of the centerline of the adjacent street and shall not have a sign area greater than 25 square feet.
(b) Other than subdivision entrance signs allowed under subsection (a) above, parcels located in residential zoning districts shall not contain signs having an aggregate sign area greater than 15 square feet. No individual sign shall exceed four square feet in sign areas in a residential zoning district. Signs having a height greater than six feet above the grade level of the centerline of the adjacent street to which the parcel is oriented are prohibited in residential zoning districts.
4.5-2 Commercial/industrial districts.
(a) Parcels may contain more than one freestanding sign, provided that:
(1) Unless otherwise stated in this ordinance, parcels exceeding three acres shall be allowed a maximum aggregate sign area of 300 square feet for the entire parcel, but no single sign shall have a display area exceeding 200 square feet.
(2) Unless otherwise stated in this ordinance, parcels less than three acres but greater than 30,000 square feet shall be allowed a maximum aggregate sign area of 128 square feet for the entire parcel.
(3) Unless otherwise stated in this ordinance, parcels less than 30,000 square feet in size shall be allowed a maximum aggregate sign area of 100 square feet for the entire parcel.
(b) Residential uses in the commercial and industrial districts shall comply with the signage requirements of subsection 4.5-1.
1175:
4.6-1 Billboard signs are allowed on commercial or industrial parcels within the interstate corridor as provided herein.
4.6-2 Size. The display area and trim of an Interstate billboard sign shall not exceed 12 feet in height and 50 [feet] in length or a display area in excess of 600 square feet. The display area and trim of a non-interstate billboard sign shall not exceed 12 feet in height and 24 feet in length or a display area in excess of 288 square feet.
4.6-3 Form and number. Billboard signs shall not be placed side-by-side or stacked. A sign at a single location, whether back-to-back or "V" formation, shall be the same height above the interstate highway surface. Not more than six billboard signs shall be permitted per quadrant of any interchange adjacent to the interstate highway.
4.6-4 Height and setback. All billboard signs shall be a minimum of ten feet above adjacent interstate highway pavement measuring from the lower portion of the sign face. Non-interstate billboard signs shall not extend more than 40 feet in height above the adjacent ground. Interstate billboard signs shall not extend more than 70 feet in height above the adjacent ground. The following rules shall apply in determining adjacent ground: If the base of the sign structure is below the grade of the adjacent roadway, the sign height is measured from the elevation of the adjacent roadway that is nearest to the sign structure. The ground shall not be altered for the sole purpose of providing additional sign height. The edge of the display area for any sign structures shall be not less than ten feet from any property or right-of-way line.
4.6-5 Spacing. Billboard signs shall be spaced a minimum of 500 feet apart measured on the same side of the roadway and from the closest point relative to each other.
4.6-6 Illumination. All illuminated signs shall use base mounted fluorescent or mercury vapor lights and shall be activated by photo-electric cells and shall be so directed as to avoid any potential traffic hazard. Additional lighting including but not limited to neon, animation and running lights are prohibited on interstate billboards. Non-interstate billboards, pylon signs and wall signs may have LED or digital displays.
4.6-7 Extrusions prohibited. Extrusions beyond the face of the sign, excluding aprons, are prohibited.
1176: Except as provided in this ordinance, all signs shall be subject to the provisions below, governing nonconforming uses. Such provisions, however, shall not be construed to prevent a legally operating nonconforming use from using signs otherwise permitted for similar conforming uses.
1177:
The lawful use of land area or sign structure existing at the time of enactment of or subsequent amendment to this ordinance may be continued subject to the following restrictions even though such use does not conform with the provisions of this ordinance.
Existing nonconforming sign structures shall not be:
(1) Changed to another nonconforming sign;
(2) Torn down and rebuilt or moved and rebuilt as a nonconforming sign;
(3) Extended or enlarged; or
(4) Rebuilt, altered, or repaired after damage exceeding 50 percent of the fair market value of the improvements, except when changed conditions beyond the control of the owner render the sign nonconforming or warrant the sign's repair.
For the purpose of administration of this provision ordinary maintenance of a sign is not deemed to be or constitute an extension or enlargement of the sign; and changing the face of the sign is not deemed a change prohibited by this section.
1178: Nonconforming signs which have been allowed to deteriorate so as to constitute either an aesthetic nuisance or a safety hazard are subject to removal pursuant to article VII of this ordinance. A sign shall be deemed to be deteriorated if the paint on its face is faded, cracked or peeling, if removable letters on the changeable copy board are missing or in disarray, if plastic panels are missing, broken or stained, if the sign face or its supporting frame work is rusty or in need of paint, if the area surrounding the sign base is not maintained and kept free of weeds and debris, or if the sign is in need of structural repair.
1179: Nonconforming signs which have been abandoned, shall be removed in their entirety by the record owner of the building or the person who obtained the sign license, whichever owns the sign or portion thereof, within 90 days after the business using the sign closes or ceases to operate on the premises where the sign is located.
1182: An applicant whose permit application has been denied or a permittee who alleges that there is error in any order, requirement, decisions, or determination made by the zoning administrator or any other administrative official in connection with the enforcement of this ordinance, may appeal the decision to the zoning board of appeals as established by article VIII of the city zoning ordinance upon filing a written notice of an appeal with the zoning administrator within ten days of the challenged decision. The board of zoning appeals shall consider an appeal at the next meeting held after the city's receipt of the written notice of appeal, provided that the notice of appeal is received a minimum of five full business days before the meeting. If the appeal is not heard at the next meeting it shall be heard at the next regular meeting of the zoning board of appeals thereafter, but in any event no later than 45 days from the date the written notice of an appeal was filed with the zoning administrator. The zoning board of appeals shall make a final decision not later than 30 days from the date of the hearing.
1183: The duly appointed zoning board of appeals shall have the power to reverse or amend the decision of the zoning administrator, and/or authorize a variance from the strict application of this ordinance where such application will result in practical difficulties or unnecessary hardships to the person owning or having the beneficial use of the property or sign for which the variance is sought.
1184:
A variance may be allowed by the board of appeals only in cases involving practical difficulties or unnecessary hardships when the evidence in the official record of the appeal supports all the following affirmative findings:
(1) That the alleged hardships or practical difficulties or both, are exceptional and peculiar to the property of the person requesting the variance, and result from conditions which do not exist generally throughout the city.
(2) That the alleged hardships and practical difficulties, or both, which will result from a failure to grant the variance, include substantially more than mere inconvenience, inability to attain a higher financial return, or both. (This is fairly standard variance language — it gives the commission a little wiggle room.)
(3) That allowing the variance will result in substantial justice being done:
a. Considering the public benefits intended to be secured by this ordinance;
b. The individual hardships that will be suffered by a failure of the board to grant a variance; and
c. The rights of others whose property would be affected by the allowance of the variance.
(4) That the requested variance is the minimum variance necessary to allow the applicant to enjoy the rights commonly enjoyed by others similarly situated.
(5) That granting of the variance would not violate more than one standard of this ordinance.
The above findings of fact shall be made by the board of appeals, which is not empowered to grant a variance without an affirmative finding of fact on the categories above. Every finding of fact shall be supported in the record of the proceedings of the board.
Nothing contained herein shall be construed to empower the board of appeals to change the terms of this ordinance or to add to the signs permitted in any district.
1185: Should the appellant wish to appeal the board's decision, the appellant must do so by writ of certiorari directly to the Superior Court of Catoosa County. There shall be no intermediate appeal to the mayor and council or any other administrative body. An application for a writ of certiorari must be filed within 30 days of the applicant's receipt of the written decision of the board.
1187:
7.1-1 A sign permit is required before a permanent or temporary/special event sign may be erected or attached to, suspended from or supported on a building or structure; and before an existing sign may be enlarged, relocated or materially improved upon to an extent of 60 percent of its total replacement value. All signs using electrical wiring and connections shall require an electrical permit.
7.1-2 A sign permit shall be issued by the code enforcement office/building inspector when the plans, specifications and intended use of the permanent sign or part thereof conform in all respects to the applicable provisions of this ordinance, the city building code, and the requirements of the electrical code as certified by the zoning administrator and a permit fee has been paid by the applicant. The administrative application shall be accompanied by plans or such other information (property lines, street names, building locations, distances from building to the road, distances to sign from road, along with a detailed drawing of the sign(s) itself) and such other information as the zoning administrator may reasonably require in the exercise of his duties. Standardized sign plans may be filed with the zoning administrator in fulfillment of this requirement, although site plans to determine the location of a sign shall be filed with each application. The zoning administrator shall process the application and either grant or deny the application within 30 business days from the date of receipt of a complete application and payment of the proper fee. The failure of zoning administrator to timely act on the application shall be deemed a grant of the application.
7.1-3 Each permit application shall contain an agreement to indemnify and save the city harmless of all damages, demands or expenses, which may in any manner be caused by the sign(s) or sign structure.
7.1-4 The city shall deny permits to applicants that submit applications for signs that either do not comply with the provisions of this ordinance, or for incomplete applications, or for applications containing false material statements. Should it be determined that a sign permit was erroneously issued, then such permit is void ab initio. Denial of a permit shall be expressed in writing by the zoning administrator before the end of the 30 business days established for review of the application and shall state the reasons for denial of the application. For the purposes of this ordinance, the communication may be made by email or facsimile. Alternatively, the city may personally serve the sign applicant with a copy of the written notice of denial within 30 business days after the city's receipt of the application. The sign applicant shall have the right to appeal the denial of a permit to the city's zoning board of appeals by written notice of appeal as provide in section 6.3 above.
7.1-5 A sign permit shall become null and void if the sign for which the permit was issued has not been completed within a period of six months after the date of issuance. No refunds will be made for permit fees paid for permits that expired due to failure to erect a permitted sign. Where a permit has expired for failure to erect the sign and a sign is later desired in the same location, a new application must be processed and another fee paid in accordance with the fee schedule in effect at the time of re-application.
1188:
7.2-1 A permit fee shall be paid to the zoning administrator for each permit required by this ordinance. The fee shall be in accordance to rate schedule maintained in the office of the city manager. No permit shall be issued until the exact dimensions and area of the sign have been filed with the zoning administrator.
7.2-2 Permit fees shall not apply to the ordinary servicing, repainting of existing sign message, cleaning of a sign, nor to changing of advertising on a sign specifically designed for periodic change of message without change in structure.
1189:
All signs, together with all their supports, braces, guys, and anchors, shall be kept in constant repair and unless constructed of galvanized or non-corroding metal, shall be periodically given a protective coating. The area immediately in front of all freestanding signs shall be maintained free of high weeds and debris. In addition to the above provisions, the zoning administrator may cause any sign or structure which:
(a) Is structurally unsafe; or
(b) Constitutes a hazard to safety or health by reason of inadequate maintenance, dilapidation or abandonment; or
(c) Is not kept in good repair; or
(d) Is capable of causing electrical shocks, to be removed following notice of 24 hours to the owner, at the expense of the owner thereof, and to destroy or otherwise dispose of the same.
1190:
If any sign is erected or maintained in violation of the provisions of this ordinance, the zoning administrator shall have the power to give the owner thereof written notice of such violation, said notice to include a brief statement of the particulars in which such violation is to be remedied. If a sign has been registered with the zoning administrator, notice to the registered owner or the person or firm receiving the permit shall be sufficient. If a sign has not been registered and the owner is not known, affixing a copy of the notice to the sign, graphic structure, or building for a period of ten days shall be sufficient. Notwithstanding the foregoing, in the interest of safety, any official or employee of the city shall have the authority to remove and dispose of any sign placed within the public right-of-way without notice to the owner.
If such a violation is not remedied within 30 days after such notice, the owner shall remove the sign immediately or be subject to a $100.00 a day fine for each day the sign remains. If the sign is not removed by the owner, the zoning administrator shall have the right to remove such sign at the expense of the owner thereof and to destroy or otherwise dispose of the same.
1191: If a new zoning district is created after the initial enactment of this ordinance or subsequent amendment, no signs shall be permitted therein until this ordinance shall be amended to include such zone district.
1193: This ordinance shall both be adopted and amended hereafter, only after the mayor and council shall have authorized the Ringgold Planning Commission or equivalent (hereafter known as the planning commission) to conduct a public hearing, then review and recommend the adoption or subsequent amendment. After conclusion of the required public hearing (section 8.2), the planning commission shall have 30 days within which to submit its written report to the mayor and council. If the planning commission fails to submit a report within the 30-day period it shall be deemed to have approved the adoption or subsequent amendment.
1194: Before enacting an amendment to this ordinance, the planning commission of the City of Ringgold, Georgia, shall hold a public hearing thereon, and at least 15 days' notice of the date, time, place, and purpose shall be published in the legal organ of Catoosa County, Georgia.
1195: After the expiration of the 30-day period within which the planning commission must act, the mayor and council of the City of Ringgold may proceed to final action on the adoption or subsequent amendment.
1196:
Footnote 1:
Editor's note— Section 1 of Ord. No. 2014-0324, adopted March 24, 2014, did not specify manner of inclusion; hence, codification as Appendix D, §§ 1-1—1-11 was at the discretion of the editor.
1197:
To insure that due process is afforded the general public of the City of Ringgold, Georgia and all parties in interest when the City of Ringgold implements and exercises zoning power pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 36-66-1 et seq., the City of Ringgold does hereby enact this Ordinance.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1198:
This Ordinance shall be known and may be cited as "The Zoning Procedures and Standards Ordinance of the City of Ringgold."
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1199:
When used in this Ordinance, the following terms are defined:
City shall mean the City of Ringgold, Georgia.
Commission shall mean the Ringgold Planning Commission or any other authority hereafter designated by the mayor and council to participate in the exercise of any zoning power and/or to provide advisory recommendations for the mayor and council relating to any zoning decision.
Conditional use or Special Use shall mean a land use which is not allowed per se in a zoning district but may be allowed only after a review, as required by this Ordinance, determines that such use is not detrimental to adjoining lands or existing land uses.
Mayor and council shall mean the mayor and council of the City which is solely responsible for the exercise of the zoning power within the municipal limits of the City and upon the annexation of lands to the municipal limits of the City.
Municipal limits shall mean the incorporated areas of the City.
Unincorporated Island shall mean the definition of unincorporated island contained in O.C.G.A. § 36-36-90 (3).
Zoning shall mean the power of the City to provide within its municipal limits for the zoning, districting, or land use regulation of property pursuant to this Ordinance and any amendment thereto.
Zoning decision shall mean the final action by the mayor and council which results in either: a) the adoption of a zoning ordinance; b) the adoption of an amendment to a zoning ordinance which changes the text of the zoning ordinance; c) the adoption of an amendment to a zoning ordinance and/or zoning map which rezones property from one zoning classification to another; d) the adoption of an ordinance annexing land into the City with a specified zoning classification; or e) the establishment of a conditional use.
Zoning ordinance shall mean an ordinance or resolution of the mayor and council or an amendment thereto by the mayor and council that either: a) regulates the location, height, bulk and size of buildings and other structures; b) regulates the use of buildings, structures, and land for business, industry, commerce, residence, public, and other purposes; c) divides lands within the corporate limits of the City into zoning districts for particular purposes and establishes their boundaries; d) provides for annexation of lands into the corporate limits of the City pursuant to such land use regulations; e) provides for a Board of Zoning Appeals and define powers and duties; f) provides for a method of zoning administration and enforcement; g) provides for amendment to the zoning ordinance and the zoning map; h) prescribes penalties for violation of the provisions of the zoning ordinance. A zoning map adopted in conjunction with a zoning ordinance which defines the zoning districts and classifications of property is included within the term "zoning ordinance."
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1200: Adoption of a zoning ordinance and zoning map shall be in accordance with the following process:
1201:
A zoning ordinance and zoning map for the City may be adopted by the mayor and council without prior submission to the Commission. Not less than one (1) public hearing shall be held by the mayor and council prior to adoption of any zoning ordinance and zoning map.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1202:
A public notice of the date, time, place and purpose of any public hearing precedent to the adoption of any zoning ordinance and zoning map shall be given not less than fifteen (15) days but not more than forty-five (45) days prior to any public hearing upon the subject of adoption of a zoning ordinance and zoning map by the mayor and council. Such public notice shall be published in the legal organ for Catoosa County, Georgia.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1203:
Any public hearing shall be called by the mayor or his designee (hereinafter the term "mayor" shall include his designee). Any person in attendance who requests to be heard concerning any matter within the text of the proposed zoning ordinance or zoning map shall be heard, subject to the rules set forth herein, after the call to order of the public hearing. The mayor shall preside at the public hearing and may recognize persons requesting to be heard. The mayor shall open any public hearing with an explanation of the purpose for the public hearing and a description of the general rules in conducting the public hearing. Any individual requesting to be heard on a matter germane to the purpose of the public hearing must be recognized by the mayor before addressing the mayor and council. Whether any comment or presentation before the mayor and council is germane to the public hearing shall be the sole determination of the mayor or his designee. The mayor is authorized to rule any person or any portion of any person's presentation out of order and not germane to the published purpose for the public hearing. Any person, upon being recognized by the mayor will give his/her name and residence address before making any comment, remark, or presentation. Any person recognized shall respond to questions from the mayor and council. The mayor may pre-determine the length of any presentation and allot equal time to proponents and opponents of the proposed zoning decision. The fact that equal time is not used by either the proponents or opponents shall not invalidate any proceeding or final action taken by the mayor and council. Provided, however, the proponents of adoption and the opponents of adoption shall be allowed a minimum aggregate time period of not less than ten (10) minutes per side for presentation of data, evidence, or opinion. Any person may present written comments concerning the proposed zoning ordinance to the mayor and council by submittal to the City Clerk not later than the close of the public hearing. Written comments submitted to the mayor and council shall become public records available for inspection upon proper request. The City Clerk will present all written comments to the mayor and council for its consideration prior to final action by the mayor and council on the proposed zoning ordinance and zoning map.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1204:
The mayor and council will consider the adoption of a proposed zoning ordinance and zoning map in a meeting or meetings open to the public called in conformity with the Georgia Open Meetings Law. The mayor and council may review, or have reviewed by staff, any modifications to the proposed zoning ordinance and zoning map prepared as a consequence of the public hearing or public comments. In enacting any proposed zoning ordinance and zoning map, the mayor and council shall apply the standards and factors enumerated in Section 1-8 of this Ordinance, as well as the future development map and policies for the City and Ringgold urban area as contained in the current and adopted comprehensive plan, as amended, of the City.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1205:
In order to accommodate the timing requirements of state law concerning the annexation of unincorporated islands, the following procedure will be used for such annexations.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1206:
Annexations of unincorporated islands, or any part thereof, to the City is accomplished by the mayor and council without prior submission to the Planning Commission. Not less than one public hearing shall be held by the mayor and council prior to the enactment of an ordinance to annex an unincorporated island or any portion thereof.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1207:
A public notice of the date, time, place and purpose of any public hearing precedent to the enactment of an ordinance to annex an unincorporated island or any portion thereof shall be given not less than fifteen (15) days but not more than forty-five (45) days prior to any public hearing upon the subject of the annexation of an unincorporated island or any portion thereof. Such public notice shall be published in the legal organ for Catoosa County, Georgia.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1208:
Any public hearing shall be called by the mayor or his designee (hereinafter the term "mayor" shall include his designee). Any person in attendance who requests to be heard concerning any matter shall be heard, subject to the rules set forth herein, after the call to order of the public hearing. The mayor shall preside at the public hearing and may recognize persons requesting to be heard. The mayor shall open any public hearing with an explanation of the purpose for the public hearing and a description of the general rules in conducting the public hearing. Any individual requesting to be heard on a matter germane to the purpose of the public hearing must be recognized by the mayor before addressing the mayor and council. Whether any comment or presentation before the mayor and council is germane to the public hearing shall be the sole determination of the mayor or his designee. The mayor is authorized to rule any person or any portion of any person's presentation out of order and not germane to the published purpose for the public hearing. Any person, upon being recognized by the mayor will give his/her name and residence address before making any comment, remark, or presentation. Any person recognized shall respond to questions from the mayor and council. The mayor may pre-determine the length of any presentation and allot equal time to proponents and opponents of the proposed annexation. The fact that equal time is not used by either the proponents or opponents shall not invalidate any proceeding or final action taken by the mayor and council. Provided, however, the proponents of annexation and the opponents of annexation shall be allowed a minimum aggregate time period of not less than ten (10) minutes per side for presentation of data, evidence, or opinion. Any person may present written comments concerning the proposed annexation to the mayor and council by submittal to the city clerk not later than the close of the public hearing. Written comments submitted to the mayor and council shall become public records available for inspection upon proper request. The city clerk will present all written comments to the mayor and council for its consideration prior to final action by the mayor and council on the proposed annexation.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1209:
The mayor and council will consider the enactment of an ordinance to annex an unincorporated island or any portion thereof at the next regular meeting of the mayor and council following the public hearing referred to above. The mayor and council may review, or have reviewed by staff, any modifications to the proposed annexation prepared as a consequence of the public hearing or public comments. In enacting any proposed ordinance to annex an unincorporated island or any portion thereof, the mayor and council shall apply the standards and factors enumerated in Section 1-8 of this Ordinance, as well as the future development map and policies for the City and Ringgold urban area as contained in the current and adopted comprehensive plan of the City.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1210:
This ordinance, the zoning ordinance and/or the zoning map may be amended from time to time and a conditional use may be established only in accordance with the following procedure:
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1211:
Amendments to this ordinance, the zoning ordinance and/or zoning map must be initiated by either the mayor and council, the Commission, or sixty (60) percent of the property owners owning not less than sixty (60) percent of the total affected lands. The interest of a property owner may be represented by a person holding a written power-of-attorney for the property owner. Consideration for conditional use permits must be initiated by the property owner or any person holding written power-of-attorney for the property owner(s).
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1212:
Except as provided in Section 1-4.1 of this Ordinance, a zoning decision shall not become effective until the amendment or application for a conditional use or annexation shall first be submitted to the Commission for review, public hearing, and advisory recommendation. All amendments shall be initiated by a written application submitted to the Commission through its professional staff member(s) upon forms provided by the Commission.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1213:
At time of submission of any application for a zoning decision, the applicant shall pay the required administrative fee then in effect pursuant to resolution of the mayor and council.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1214:
Public notice shall be given of a public hearing on any proposed zoning decision as hereinafter provided.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1215:
No less than fifteen (15) days but not more than forty-five (45) days before the date set for public hearing, notice shall be given to the general public of the proposed zoning decision stating the date, time, place, and purpose of the public hearing. The notice shall be published in the legal organ for Catoosa County, Georgia.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1216:
Where the proposed zoning amendment requests the rezoning of property or the initial zoning of property to be annexed or consideration of a conditional use these additional procedures are applicable:
(a) The published notice shall include the location of the property and state the current zoning classification of the property and the proposed zoning classification of the property, if applicable;
(b) If a matter that constitutes a zoning decision is initiated by a party other than the mayor and council, a sign, not less than 17 inches by 24 inches, shall be placed by staff of the Commission in a conspicuous location on the property sought to be rezoned and/or considered for annexation or conditional use permit setting forth the date, time, place, and purpose of the public hearing, the present zoning classification of the property, if applicable, and the proposed classification or conditional use of the property, as applicable. Acts of vandalism or natural occurrence diminishing the effectiveness of notice by the sign posted on the property shall not invalidate any proceeding of final action taken on the proposed zoning decision.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1217:
The Commission and the Mayor and Council shall each conduct a separate public hearing on any proposed zoning decision other than as provided in Sections 1-4 and 1-4A of this Ordinance. Although the planning commission will convene a public hearing on each proposal, the official public hearing will be held by the city council. The public hearings shall be conducted on the date and at the time and place specified by the Commission and the Mayor and Council. The purpose of such public hearings is to enable the proponent of the zoning decision to present the proposal before the general public and to receive comments on the proposed zoning decision from interested persons and the general public. The Commission and the Mayor and Council shall consider germane comments presented by the proponent of the zoning decision and by interested persons and the general public at such public hearing prior to the Commission making its advisory recommendation to the mayor and council, and the Mayor and Council shall consider the same and the recommendation of the Commission prior to making a final zoning decision. Zoning standards and factors as enumerated in Section 1-8 or Section 1-9 of this Ordinance, as applicable, shall be applied by the Commission and the Mayor and Council in making its advisory recommendation to the mayor and council and the final zoning decision, respectively. The Commission and the Mayor and Council shall prescribe rules of order for its conduct of public hearings pursuant to this section and shall be consistent with the general requirements and purposes set forth in this Ordinance and the general laws of the State of Georgia concerning the conduct of proceedings by municipal authorities. The following procedures (Section 1-7.1 through Section 1-7.9) shall govern the conduct of hearings and other proceedings before the Commission and the Mayor and Council, and the reference to the Chairman of the Commission shall also be applicable to the mayor or his designee in conducting the public hearing before the Mayor and Council.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1218:
The Chairman of the Commission or his designee on the Commission (hereinafter either may be referred to as the "Chairman") shall open any public hearing with an explanation of the purpose for the public hearing and a description of the general rules of the Commission for conducting the public hearing. Any individual requesting to be heard on the matter germane to the purpose of the public hearing must be recognized by the Chairman before addressing the Commission. Whether any comment or presentation to the Commission is germane to the public hearing shall be the sole determination of the Chairman. The Chairman is authorized to rule any person or any portion of any person's presentation out of order and not germane to the published purpose of the public hearing. Any person addressing the Commission, upon being recognized by the Chairman, shall give his/her name and residence address before making any comment, remark, or presentation. Any person addressing the Commission shall respond to questions from any member of the Commission. The Chairman may pre-determine the length of any hearing and shall allot equal time to proponents and opponents of any proposed zoning amendment and/or conditional use for presentation of data, evidence, and opinion. The fact that equal time is not in fact used by either the proponents or opponents shall not invalidate any proceeding or final action taken on the proposed amendment and/or conditional use. Provided, however, that the proponents and opponents of the issue before the Commission shall be allowed a minimum aggregate time period of not less than ten (10) minutes per side for the presentation of data, evidence or opinion.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1219:
The Chairman shall determine whether any application for zoning amendment or conditional use is properly initiated and the type of zoning decision called for by the application. The Chairman shall announce at the outset of any public hearing whether the application is in proper order for consideration by the Commission.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1220:
The Chairman shall allow the proponent of the proposed zoning amendment or conditional use to provide an explanation or description of the proposed zoning amendment or conditional use and the reason(s) for initiating the proposed zoning amendment or conditional use. The presence of an annexation applicant at the public hearing is not required, unless the petition was filed using the sixty (60) percent method or the zone district requested in the annexation application requires the presentation and approval of a site plan. However, the applicant for a proposed zoning amendment or conditional use, or his attorney at law or in fact, must be present at the public hearing to present the merits of the application. The failure of an applicant or his legal representative to attend the public hearing will result in the Commission making an unfavorable advisory recommendation on the application to the mayor and council.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1221:
The Chairman shall enter into the record the contents of any pertinent written comment, petition or written statement, plat, photograph or other documentary evidence received by the Commission in support of the proposed zoning amendment or conditional use. Such written comments, petitions or other documentary evidence or exhibits shall be considered a part of the record by the Commission and may be considered by the Commission in making its advisory recommendation to the mayor and council.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1222:
The Chairman shall then permit persons opposed to the proposed zoning amendment or conditional use an opportunity to address the Commission in the public hearing in accordance with the rules of the Commission and the allocation of time announced at the commencement of the public hearing.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1223:
The Chairman may alternate the presentation of persons speaking in favor or in opposition to the proposed zoning amendment or conditional use beginning with the presentation of the proponent or his/her attorney at law or in fact, or the Chairman may divide such presentation into blocks of time beginning with the proponents of the proposed zoning amendment or conditional use and moving thereafter to the presentation of the opponents of the proposed zoning amendment. Further, the Chairman may direct that the proponents and opponents designate one or more spokesperson(s) for the presentation of views on a proposed zoning amendment or conditional use. The Chairman may poll the public assemblage at the hearing concerning the concurrence and/or opposition with remarks of any person addressing the Commission at the public hearing.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1224:
Any remark amounting to an attack on the character or personal integrity of another person, not actually supportable in law or fact, or in the form of an emotional outburst shall be deemed non-germane to the purpose of public hearing and shall be ruled out of order. The Commission shall have the power to remove from the hearing room or censor any person who continues to make such non-germane remarks after being ruled out of order.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1225:
Upon conclusion of the presentation of persons opposing the proposed zoning amendment or conditional use, the Chairman shall offer the proponent of the zoning amendment or proponent's designee a specified amount of time to address the Commission in rebuttal of any issue raised by persons addressing the Commission in opposition to the proposed zoning amendment or conditional use. The Chairman shall rule out of order any new issue raised in rebuttal unless deemed useful to the Commission in evaluating the merits of the proposed zoning amendment or conditional use. If a new issue is allowed to be raised by rebuttal then persons opposing the proposed zoning amendment shall be allotted an equal amount of time through one or more spokesperson(s) to address the new issue(s).
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1226:
When proponents and opponents of the proposed zoning amendment or conditional use have been heard in accordance with the foregoing procedure, the Chairman shall declare the public hearing closed. No further public hearing on the issue shall be required prior to the advisory recommendation of the Commission to the mayor and council or prior to the taking of final action on the proposed zoning amendment or conditional use by the mayor and council.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1227:
Exercise of zoning power by the mayor and council shall constitute an effort to balance the interest of the City in promoting the public health, safety, morality, and/or general welfare against the right of property owners to the unrestricted use of their property.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1228:
The following factors are determined to be relevant in balancing the interests in promoting the public health, safety, morality, and/or general welfare against the right to unrestricted use of property:
a) Whether the proposed amendment would allow a use that is generally suitable for the site compared to other possible uses and the uses and zoning of adjacent and nearby properties.
b) Whether the proposed amendment would adversely affect the economic value or the uses of adjacent, abutting, and nearby properties.
c) Whether the extent to which the destruction or diminishing of the value of the lot or parcel proposed for zoning amendment promotes the health, safety, morals, or general welfare of the public.
d) Whether the property to be affected by the proposed amendment can be used as currently zoned considering the suitability of the subject lot or parcel for the proposed zoned purposes.
e) Whether the relative gain to the general public, as compared to the hardship imposed upon the owner of the subject lot or parcel under the current zoning substantially promotes the general welfare of the public.
f) The length of time the property has been vacant as zoned, considered in the context of land development in the area and in the vicinity of the proposed land to be rezoned.
g) Whether the lot or parcel sought to be rezoned/annexed under the proposed amendment is in conformity or divergence with the policy and intent of the adopted Joint Comprehensive Plan/equivalent, as amended.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1229:
The mayor and council and the Commission, in its advisory recommendation to the Mayor and council, shall consider the proposed zoning amendment or conditional use in light of the factors set forth in Section 1-8 or Section 1-9, as applicable. In evaluating the factors set forth in Section 1-8 it shall be the policy of the City to exercise its zoning power in conformity with the adopted policies and intent of the current and adopted comprehensive plan of the City, insofar as the plan is current in its application to development patterns in the area sought to be zoned or rezoned. The policy of the City is to exercise its zoning power for purposes of assuring the compatibility of usage of adjacent and nearby properties and the preservation of the economic value of adjacent and nearby properties, while enabling a use of all properties measured by the U.S. Constitution and the Georgia Constitution.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1230:
The granting of a conditional use does not constitute a permanent change in zoning or use. The conditional use can be forfeited if it does not meet the review criteria. To ameliorate the impact of a conditional use on surrounding property, no conditional use may be granted without special provisions for conditions, criteria, standards, and/or requirements as to the particular use.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1232:
The procedure for considering any proposed zoning amendment or conditional use that is properly initiated and subsequent to the required public hearing shall be as follows:
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1233:
The Commission shall make an advisory recommendation to the mayor and council as to the adoption of any proposed zoning amendment or conditional use. The recommendation of the Commission shall be in writing and addressed to the mayor and council and will clearly state the Commission's recommendation on the proposed zoning amendment or conditional use. The Commission's recommendation shall provide evaluation of each of the factors set forth in Section 1-8 or 1-9, as applicable, and describe how the Commission's recommendation is consistent with those factors for the exercise of the zoning power of the City. A summary of the proceedings of the public hearing or transcript thereof along with the record of the proceeding before the Commission shall accompany the Commission's written recommendation to the mayor and council.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1234:
Upon conclusion of the public hearing before the Commission, the Commission may make a recommendation to either approve, disapprove, or table the proposed zoning amendment or conditional use. If consideration of the proposed zoning amendment or conditional use is tabled, it shall be reconsidered by the Commission not later than sixty (60) days after the close of the public hearing. If the Commission tables their recommendation, then the scheduled public hearing of the mayor and council may continue, however the mayor and council shall await the recommendation of the commission before taking final action. The rules of the Commission shall provide for a regular monthly meeting during each calendar month. If no advisory recommendation is submitted to the mayor and council within sixty (60) days of the close of the public hearing on any zoning amendment or conditional use, the Commission shall be deemed to have made a favorable recommendation of the proposed zoning amendment or conditional use. The application for zoning amendment or conditional use shall not be withdrawn once the Commission opens and conducts the public hearing. The Commission shall make a recommendation to the mayor and council on the proposed zoning amendment or conditional use regardless whether the proponent of the zoning amendment or conditional use attempts to, thereafter, withdraw his/her application of the zoning amendment or conditional use.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1235:
The Commission's authority in any zoning decision shall only be advisory. All zoning decisions shall be made by the mayor and council and it shall either approve or disapprove the proposed zoning amendment or conditional use. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, any approval of a proposed zoning amendment or conditional use may be subject to any and all lawful conditions that may be required by the mayor and council as a condition of the approval of the proposed zoning amendment or conditional use.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1236:
If the mayor and council takes any official action disapproving a proposed zoning amendment or conditional use that same tract or parcel of land may not be considered as part of any future application until six (6) months have expired from the date of final action of the mayor and council.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
1237:
Copies of this Ordinance, as amended, shall be printed by the City and made available for distribution of the general public in the office of the City Clerk, and the office of the Code Enforcement Officer of the City. Distribution to any member of the general public shall be upon request of such person who shall be entitled to one copy. The city clerk is authorized to print copies of this Ordinance from time to time for purposes of compliance with the requirements of Georgia law.
This ordinance may also be viewed at the official city website or a link thereof.
(Ord. No. 2014-0324, § 1, 3-24-14)
